description: Minimize total part count — challenge whether each part is truly independent
look_for: Parts that could potentially be combined into a single component without losing function
pass_criteria: Each part in the assembly has a clear functional reason to be separate (different material, relative motion, or assembly/service access requirement)
fail_criteria: Two or more adjacent parts that could be combined into one part without affecting function, material requirements, or serviceability
source: Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA methodology — minimum part count criteria
fix_hint: Consider combining adjacent parts that share material and have no relative motion. Use boolean .union() to merge parts.

description: Parts should self-locate via geometric features (chamfers, pins, shoulders, bosses)
look_for: Mating interfaces between parts — do they have alignment features like shoulders, pins, chamfers, or bosses?
pass_criteria: Parts have visible self-locating features (shoulders, bosses, pins, chamfers) that guide them into correct position during assembly
fail_criteria: Parts mate on flat surfaces with no alignment features, requiring a jig or precise manual positioning
fix_hint: Add alignment bosses or shoulders to mating surfaces: .faces("selector").workplane().circle(pin_r).extrude(pin_h) for locating pins.

description: Avoid flexible, fragile, or slippery parts that are difficult to handle and orient
look_for: Thin flat parts (gaskets, shims), long slender parts (springs, wires), or parts with no graspable features
pass_criteria: All parts have adequate rigidity and graspable surfaces for manual or robotic handling
fail_criteria: Any part that would be difficult to pick up, orient, or insert due to flexibility, fragility, or lack of gripping surfaces
source: Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA — part handling difficulty analysis
fix_hint: Increase part rigidity by adding thickness or reinforcement ribs. Ensure graspable surfaces for handling.

description: Design for top-down assembly so gravity assists part insertion
look_for: Assembly sequence — can parts be added from above (Z-axis insertion) rather than from the side or below?
pass_criteria: The majority of parts can be inserted from above, with gravity holding them in place before fastening
fail_criteria: Parts that must be inserted from below or held in place against gravity during fastening, requiring extra hands or fixtures
source: DFA principles — gravity-assisted assembly reduces fixture requirements
fix_hint: Orient the assembly so parts can be inserted from above (Z-axis). Design mating features to allow gravity-assisted placement.

description: Sufficient clearance around fasteners for wrench/driver access
look_for: Bolt heads, nut locations, screw heads — is there physical space for a wrench, socket, or screwdriver?
pass_criteria: All fastener locations have visible clearance for standard tools (socket wrench, Allen key, screwdriver) to approach and turn
fail_criteria: Any fastener location where adjacent geometry would prevent a standard tool from engaging the fastener head
source: DFA — tool access clearance for fastener installation and service
fix_hint: Ensure clearance around bolt heads: at least 1.5x wrench size in all directions. Use .cboreHole() for recessed fasteners if space is tight.

description: Avoid requiring part reorientation during the assembly sequence
look_for: Whether the assembly must be flipped, rotated, or repositioned between assembly steps
pass_criteria: The assembly can be completed in one orientation (or with minimal reorientation)
fail_criteria: The assembly requires multiple flips or rotations to install different parts, adding handling time and fixture complexity
fix_hint: Design the assembly sequence so all parts can be installed from one direction (top-down). Minimize required fixture reorientations.

description: Standardize fastener types — minimize unique fastener count
look_for: Different sizes, types, or grades of fasteners used across the assembly
pass_criteria: The assembly uses no more than 2-3 unique fastener types (e.g., all M6 hex bolts and M6 nuts)
fail_criteria: More than 3 unique fastener types or sizes (e.g., mixing M4, M6, M8 bolts with different head types), increasing inventory and tool changes
source: DFA — fastener standardization reduces assembly time and error
fix_hint: Use the same bolt size throughout. Standardize on M4, M5, or M6 for all fastener locations.

description: Interference fits and press fits should have lead-in chamfers for guided insertion
look_for: Shaft-bore interfaces, pin insertions, press-fit connections between parts
pass_criteria: All press-fit or close-tolerance insertions have visible lead-in chamfers on at least one mating part
fail_criteria: Any press-fit interface where both the shaft and bore have sharp edges with no chamfer, making insertion difficult and risking damage
source: Assembly engineering — chamfered lead-ins for guided insertion
fix_hint: Add lead-in chamfers on shafts (.chamfer(0.5)) and bores (.chamfer(0.5)) for guided insertion of press-fit connections.

description: Assembly mating surfaces must be unobstructed by other parts or features
look_for: Mating faces and insertion paths — can each part reach its final position without colliding with already-assembled parts?
pass_criteria: Each part has a clear, unobstructed path to its final assembly position
fail_criteria: Any part whose insertion path is blocked by a previously assembled part, requiring disassembly or impossible assembly sequences
fix_hint: Verify that each part has a clear linear insertion path to its final position. No part should need to curve around another to reach its seat.

description: Bolt patterns should have consistent, standard spacing for common tools
look_for: Groups of bolts or screws — are they evenly spaced? Do they follow standard patterns (circular, rectangular)?
pass_criteria: Bolt patterns use consistent spacing that accommodates standard wrench sizes without interference between adjacent fasteners
fail_criteria: Irregular bolt spacing where adjacent fasteners are too close for simultaneous tool access, or spacing that requires custom tooling
source: DFA — fastener pattern design for tool clearance and consistency
fix_hint: Use regular bolt patterns with consistent spacing. Use .rarray(spacing_x, spacing_y, count_x, count_y) for uniform patterns.

pass_criteria: Fasteners are flush with the surface, protected by a cap, or the recesses are self-draining.
fail_criteria: Fasteners are located in deep, open recesses where dirt, water, or ice can accumulate and block tool access.
look_for: Deep pockets, recesses, or counterbores around fasteners that are open to the environment.
description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Avoid features that trap debris and hinder service access to fasteners.

pass_criteria: The method for joining each part to the assembly is visually identifiable (e.g., visible bolt heads, weld symbols, threaded connections).
look_for: Interfaces between parts to see if fasteners, welds, threads, or other joining methods are shown.
description: [RETIRED — triage: out_of_scope] Assembly method between components must be clearly defined.
fail_criteria: Parts are shown mated together with no visible or indicated means of attachment, making the assembly method ambiguous.

description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Gears and pulleys mounted on shafts must have an explicit axial retention feature (shoulder + retaining-ring groove, shaft nut, or set screw).
look_for: A rotating disc on a plain shaft with no groove, shoulder, threaded end, or set-screw boss to stop axial walk-off.
pass_criteria: Every hub-on-shaft joint shows at least one positive axial stop plus a removable/permanent retainer.
fail_criteria: A gear/hub sits on a plain cylindrical shaft with no visible means of preventing it from sliding off.

description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Torque-transmitting hub-shaft joints must include a rotational drive feature (keyway, spline, D-flat, or specified press fit).
look_for: A round bore on a round shaft carrying load with no key, flat, or spline to transmit torque.
pass_criteria: The interface shows a key/spline/D-flat or is explicitly annotated as an interference fit sized for the torque.
fail_criteria: A load-bearing gear rides a plain round shaft with no rotational lock, relying on friction alone.

description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Meshing gear pairs must be placed at center distance = sum of pitch radii, verified against tooth geometry to avoid interference.
look_for: Overlap of the two gears' tooth profiles at the mesh beyond normal single-tooth engagement.
pass_criteria: Tooth tips of one gear clear the root of the other with visible backlash; center distance matches pitch radii.
fail_criteria: Addendum circles overlap so far that teeth appear to collide/interpenetrate, indicating too-small center distance.

description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Any threaded joint tightened against a rotatable member must provide a counter-hold feature (wrench flats, hex, spanner slots) accessible from the same side as the fastener.
look_for: The exposed end of the rotating shaft beyond the nut — does it show flats, a hex, or spanner holes, or is it a plain cylinder?
pass_criteria: A counter-hold feature is present and reachable from the same approach direction as the nut.
fail_criteria: The shaft end is plain round, forcing reaction torque through blades, vanes, belts, or a second-side tool access.

description: [RETIRED — triage: legacy_low_evidence] Rotating open impellers, fans, or wheels must be guarded or shrouded, or the design must document an enclosing casing supplied at the next assembly level.
look_for: Whether the bladed rotor is fully exposed on the free side in the isometric and axial views, with no casing, cover, or guard geometry present.
pass_criteria: A casing/shroud encloses the blade sweep, or a guard mounting interface (bolt bosses, register diameter) exists on the mount plate.
fail_criteria: An open bladed rotor is exposed at operator height with no guard geometry and no visible provision for mounting one.
